listing.name: JetStrike / SDL3 Port
listing.summary: Play DOS JetStrike with the SDL3 port, using the Windows package or a Linux source build and your own CD-ROM data.

steps.title: Prepare a writable copy of your original game
steps.instruction: Use your own DOS CD-ROM installation. Keep JS_CDROM.EXE and the INTRO, DATA, GFX, MAP, MISC and PLANE directories together in a writable Game copy.

steps.title: Use the upstream Windows setup
steps.instruction: Extract the complete Windows x64 ZIP into its own folder and keep both executables and every DLL together. Open JetStrike.exe to choose your data and options. The optional Rip CD music action uses your owned CUE image and writes the 14 audio tracks under Game/MUSIC.

steps.title: Build the direct player on Linux
steps.instruction: The reviewed release has no Linux package. Use the upstream source with a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and SDL3 development files. From the repository root, run cmake -S jsport -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DJS_LAUNCHER=OFF -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD_LIBRARIES=-lm, then cmake --build build --target jsport. Keep the built jsport and its SDL3 runtime available. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used on Linux. This build has not been tested with original CD-ROM data on Linux.

steps.title: Register the actual player in Portcove
steps.instruction: On Windows, choose jsport.exe as the existing installation; on Linux, choose the built jsport. Choose the player’s containing directory as the working directory. Add --game-dir and your writable Game copy as two separate arguments. Review the selected player, folder and arguments, then choose Play. The separate upstream launcher can stay open or close while its game continues.

warnings: Use your own original game files. The native port includes reconstructed original program behavior and its own separately licensed port code.

references.title: Keep your settings and progress before replacing files
references.instruction: Back up JS.CFG, js_save.000 through js_save.009 and any MUSIC folder with your working game data. Copy %APPDATA%/JetStrike/settings.ini as well. Close both the player and launcher before replacing files. Portcove keeps a launch registration. You and upstream own runtime replacement and backups. Removing the registration leaves the working files and profile in place.

references.title: Other platforms
references.instruction: Windows x64 has the reviewed official package. Linux x64 uses the upstream source build described above, with no reviewed Linux package or title-run evidence. Intel Mac and Apple Silicon have no reviewed package or native build evidence. Android has no reviewed package or mobile host integration. Those platforms do not inherit Windows or Linux observations.
